_comment: DBE Grade 12 Mathematical Literacy P1, November 2025. Questions + marking-memo
answers extracted by reading the rendered scanned question paper (no text layer)
and the bilingual (Afrikaans/English) Marking Guidelines PDF (text layer present).
Only the ENGLISH memo content is transcribed. solution_method is the method the
MEMO uses to solve each question - this is the content signal the matcher links
against, not the surface wording of the question. memo_answer is verbatim from
the guidelines (decimal commas kept, South African convention).
CONTEXT CONVENTION: Mathematical Literacy questions hang off shared scenario/
resource boxes. The full scenario (tables/graphs/plans described in bracketed
words) is transcribed verbatim inside the text of the FIRST sub-question of each
block, prefixed 'CONTEXT for ...'. Later sub-questions carry a short pointer.
ANNEXURE NOTE: From 2025 the annexures/answer sheets are printed inside a
17-page SPECIAL ANSWER BOOK which is NOT in the repo. This paper references
ANNEXURE A (monthly PAYE deduction table + 2024/2025 annual tax rates),
ANSWER SHEET 3.2 (stacked bar graph of LTE devices per province, 2021-2023)
and ANNEXURE B (average petrol price per month in pounds, four months of 2024).
Annexure-dependent data below is RECONSTRUCTED from the values the memo uses;
such questions carry '[ANNEXURE ... in Special Answer Book - not in repo]' in
their text and checkable:false where the reading itself cannot be verified.
To be verified when the answer book arrives (queue row exists).

questions.text: CONTEXT for 1.1 (Q1.1.1-1.1.4): TABLE 1 below shows the prices of some food items in three cities of South Africa, namely Johannesburg, Durban and Cape Town. Rows: Salt 1 kg R18,07 | R17,16 | R10,24; Onions # 10 kg R111,59 | R100,58 | R104,10; Carrots # 5 kg R41,41 | R39,63 | R35,08; Butternuts # 10 kg R105,24 | R90,04 | R96,91; Curry powder 200 g R41,91 | R34,24 | R39,82; White sugar 10 kg R223,23 | R197,07 | R229,49; Apples 3 kg R52,38 | R54,73 | R46,31; Oranges 7 kg R104,96 | R78,80 | R86,64; Eggs # 60 eggs R163,31 | R169,62 | R165,52; Canned beans 410 g x 6 R101,94 | R84,46 | R81,94; TOTAL (Johannesburg column): ...] [Adapted from www.businesstech.co.za] NOTE: # indicates zero-rated VAT items. questions.text: [Context 1.1: TABLE 1 food prices in three cities - see Q1.1.1] Determine, as a unit ratio rounded to THREE decimal places, the price of eggs in Cape Town compared to the price of eggs in Durban in the form 1 : ...
questions.memo_note: Memo explanation column prints '1RT 169,92' - typo for 169,62; the solution column uses 169,62. 169,62/165,52 = 1,02477... which rounds to 1,025 at three decimal places.

questions.text: CONTEXT for 2.1 (Q2.1.1-2.1.4): In South Africa, employees need to pay income tax based on their earnings. An extract of Muriel Davids' salary slip for one month for the tax year ending February 2025 is shown below. Some information has been omitted. [Salary slip: INTERNATIONAL COMPUTER SPECIALISTS PTY LTD. EMPLOYEE DETAILS: EMPLOYEE NAME M DAVIDS; AGE 42 YEARS. PAYMENTS: GROSS SALARY R35 000. EMPLOYEE DEDUCTIONS: UIF R177,12; PAYE TAX A; MEDICAL AID R2 531,54; NET SALARY B. EMPLOYER CONTRIBUTIONS: UIF R177,12; MEDICAL AID ...] Muriel does not contribute to a pension fund; hence her gross salary is her taxable income. She pays the medical aid for herself only and receives no bonus. ANNEXURE A in the ANSWER BOOK shows the monthly PAYE deduction table and the annual tax rates for the 2024/2025 tax year. [ANNEXURE A in Special Answer Book - not in repo. From memo usage it contains: a monthly PAYE deduction table giving a monthly PAYE tax of R6 298 for Muriel's salary level, and the 2024/2025 annual tax rates including bracket 'R77 362 + 31% of taxable income above R370 500', primary rebate R17 235 and a monthly medical tax credit of R364 for the taxpayer.] Use ANNEXURE A and the information above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION: Write the acronym UIF in words.
questions.memo_working: 2A correct acronym

questions.text: [Context 2.1: Muriel Davids' salary slip, ANNEXURE A - see Q2.1.1] Name the institution that collects tax on behalf of the government of South Africa.
questions.memo_answer: SARS OR South African Revenue Services
questions.memo_working: 2A correct government institution

questions.text: [Context 2.1: Muriel Davids' salary slip - see Q2.1.1] Determine the employer contribution towards the medical aid if the employer contributes one third of the total contribution.
questions.memo_working: Employer Medical Aid contribution = R2 531,54 ÷ 2 (1MA divide by 2) = R1 265,77 (1A simplification). OR Total contribution = 3/2 x R2 531,54 = R3 797,31; employer = R3 797,31 ÷ 3 OR R3 797,31 - R2 531,54 = R1 265,77. AO
questions.memo_note: The employee pays two thirds (R2 531,54), so the employer's one third equals half of the employee's deduction.

questions.text: [Context 2.1: Muriel Davids' salary slip, ANNEXURE A - see Q2.1.1] (a) Write down the missing value A from the monthly PAYE deduction table in ANNEXURE A. [ANNEXURE A in Special Answer Book - not in repo]
questions.memo_working: 2RT correct value
questions.memo_note: Pure reading from the monthly PAYE deduction table in the missing Special Answer Book; value cannot be independently verified until the answer book arrives.

questions.text: [Context 2.1: Muriel Davids' salary slip - see Q2.1.1] (b) Calculate the missing value B.
questions.memo_working: B = Gross salary - UIF - PAYE Tax - medical aid = R35 000 - R177,12 - R6 298 - R2 531,54 (1MCA subtracting values) = R25 993,34 (1CA simplification). OR B = R35 000 - (R177,12 + R6 298 + R2 531,54) = R35 000 - R9 006,66 = R25 993,34. AO. CA from Question 2.1.4(a)

questions.text: [Context 2.1: Muriel Davids' salary slip, ANNEXURE A - see Q2.1.1] (c) Muriel stated that she overpaid tax in the 2024/2025 tax year. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether her statement is VALID.
questions.topic: Finance (income tax calculation with rebates and medical credits)
questions.memo_answer: Annual taxable income = R420 000; annual tax payable after rebates = R71 104,00; monthly tax payable = R5 925,33 (or annual PAYE deducted = R6 298 x 12 = R75 576). Her statement is VALID.
questions.memo_working: Annual taxable income = R35 000 x 12 = R420 000 (1A). Annual tax payable before rebates = R77 362 + 31%(R420 000 - R370 500) (1MCA correct tax bracket) = R77 362 + R15 345 = R92 707,00 (1CA). Annual tax payable after rebates = R92 707,00 - R17 235 (1RT correct tax rebate) - (R364 x 12) = R92 707,00 - R17 235 - R4 368 (1MA subtracting MTC) = R71 104,00 (1CA). Monthly tax payable = R71 104,00 ÷ 12 = R5 925,33 OR Annual tax paid = R6 298 x 12 = R75 576 (1CA tax amount; CA from Question 2.1.4(a)). Her statement is VALID (1O conclusion).
questions.memo_note: Tax bracket values (R77 362 + 31% above R370 500), rebate R17 235 and medical credit R364/month are as printed in the memo; the annexure itself is in the missing Special Answer Book. Arithmetic verified: R75 576 deducted vs R71 104 payable, so she overpaid.

questions.text: CONTEXT for 2.2 (Q2.2.1-2.2.4): Muriel Davids travels to work by bus. TABLE 4 below shows information on the Metrobus service in Johannesburg for three categories of passengers travelling by bus. [TABLE 4: INFORMATION ON THE METROBUS SERVICE. Passenger categories: Adults (15-59 years), Children (3-14 years), Pensioners (60+ years). Rows (Trip Package | Duration | Adult trip fare | Children trip fare | Pensioner trip fare): 1 trip Daily R14,20 | R10,30 | R4,20; 10 trips Weekly R106,00 | R76,40 | -; 12 trips Weekly R127,10 | - | -; 44 trips Monthly R465,60 | R336,30 | -.] [Adapted from www.mbus.joburg.org.za] Use TABLE 4 and the information above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION: Calculate the percentage savings a pensioner receives per bus trip when compared to the amount paid by an adult for the same bus trip.
questions.memo_working: % paid = R4,20/R14,20 x 100% (1MA dividing correct values) = 29,58% (1A simplification); % savings = 100% - 29,58% = 70,42% (1CA simplification). OR % savings = (R14,20 - R4,20)/R14,20 x 100% (1MA subtracting correct values, 1A correct denominator) = 70,42% (1CA simplification)

questions.text: [Context 2.2: TABLE 4 Metrobus service - see Q2.2.1] Determine the amount Muriel will save per trip if she buys the monthly package instead of the daily trip package.
questions.memo_working: Cost per trip = R465,60/44 (1RT R465,60, 1MA dividing by 44) = R10,58 (1CA simplification). Saving per trip = R14,20 - R10,58 (1MCA subtracting values) = R3,62 (1CA simplification). OR Total cost = R14,20 x 44 = R624,80; difference = R624,80 - R465,60 = R159,20; saving per trip = R159,20/44 = R3,62

questions.text: [Context 2.2: TABLE 4 Metrobus service - see Q2.2.1] Write down the probability of a 10-year old child purchasing a weekly package with 12 trips.
questions.memo_working: 2A correct probability. The 12-trip weekly package has no child fare, so the event is impossible.

questions.text: [Context 2.2: TABLE 4 Metrobus service - see Q2.2.1] Johannesburg Metrobus introduced a compulsory card payment system. All passengers will be required to purchase the Metrobus card for R35 to activate the card. They will then have to upload trip fares according to the different available trip packages. Muriel purchased a Metrobus card together with an uploaded trip package to the total value of R416,30. Calculate the maximum number of weekly trips Muriel can take using this card.
questions.memo_working: Package amount left = R416,30 - R35,00 (1RT R35) = R381,30 (1A simplification). Number of weekly trips = R381,30 ÷ R127,10 (1MCA dividing values) = 3 (1CA simplification). OR R416,30 - R127,10 - R127,10 - R127,10 (1RT R127,10, 1MA subtracting values) = R35 (1A), so 3 (1CA)
questions.memo_note: The memo interprets 'weekly trips' as the number of 12-trip weekly packages (R127,10 each) that fit into the remaining R381,30, giving 3.

questions.text: CONTEXT for 3.1 (Q3.1.1-3.1.3): Social media platforms enable users to share information and ideas virtually through texts, photographs, videos and much more. Rows: Facebook 57% | 1 732,8 | 43% | 1 307,2; Instagram 51% | 1 020 | 49% | 980; Snapchat 46% | *** | 54% | 405; X/Twitter 56% | 346,64 | 44% | 272,36; TikTok 43% | 645 | 57% | 855; YouTube 54% | 1 350 | 46% | 1 150.] [Adapted from www.statista.com, www.datareportal.com] Use TABLE 5 and the information above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION: Calculate the median percentage for male social media users.
questions.memo_working: Arranged: 43% 46% 51% 54% 56% 57% (1MA arranging values). Median = (51% + 54%)/2 (1RT 51% and 54%, 1MA concept of median) = 52,5% (1CA simplification). AO

questions.text: [Context 3.1: TABLE 5 social media platforms - see Q3.1.1] Determine, as a decimal, the probability of randomly selecting a social media platform where the female users were fewer than the male users.
questions.memo_working: P = 4/6 (1A numerator, 1A denominator) = 0,67 (1CA simplification)
questions.memo_note: Platforms with fewer female than male users: Facebook, Instagram, X/Twitter, YouTube (4 of the 6).

questions.text: [Context 3.1: TABLE 5 social media platforms - see Q3.1.1] Fezeka is interested in the number of male and female Snapchat users. (a) Determine the total number of Snapchat users.
questions.memo_working: Total = 405 000 000 x 100/54 (1MA percentage calculation) = 750 000 000 (1CA simplification). OR male users = 46/54 x 405 000 000 = 345 000 000 (1A); total = 405 000 000 + 345 000 000 = 750 000 000 (1CA). AO

questions.text: [Context 3.1: TABLE 5 social media platforms - see Q3.1.3a] (b) Fezeka stated that the difference between the number of female and male Snapchat users was 61 300 000. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether her statement is VALID.
questions.memo_answer: Male users = 345 000 000; difference = 405 000 000 - 345 000 000 = 60 000 000. Her statement is NOT VALID.
questions.memo_working: Male users = 750 000 000 x 46/100 (1MCA calculating 46%) = 345 000 000 (1CA). Difference = 405 000 000 - 345 000 000 = 60 000 000 (1CA difference). NOT VALID (1O conclusion). OR percentage difference = 54% - 46% = 8% (1CA); 8% x 750 million (1MCA) = 60 000 000 (1CA); NOT VALID (1O). CA from Question 3.1.3(a)

questions.text: CONTEXT for 3.2 (Q3.2.1-3.2.4): There has been an increase in the number of long-term evolution (LTE) devices in South Africa over the last three years. ANSWER SHEET 3.2 in the ANSWER BOOK shows a graph for the number of LTE devices per province over a three-year period. Some of the information on the graph has been omitted. NOTE: LTE is a term used for a particular type of 4G that delivers a fast mobile internet experience. [ANSWER SHEET 3.2 in Special Answer Book - not in repo. From memo usage: a stacked (compound) bar graph, one bar per province (nine provinces including Limpopo LP, North West NW, Mpumalanga MP, Eastern Cape EC, KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng), each bar stacked by year 2021/2022/2023, vertical axis number of devices with gridlines every 10 000 000 up to 60 000 000. Memo-implied readings: Limpopo 2021 = 4 000 000, cumulative after 2022 = 11 000 000, full stack 18 500 000 (2023 = 7 500 000); highest 2021 value = 16 000 000, lowest 2021 value = 1 000 000; Limpopo and North West had equal 2021 values, as did Mpumalanga and Eastern Cape; KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumalanga bars incomplete (2023 values omitted).] Use ANSWER SHEET 3.2 and the information above to answer the questions that follow. questions.text: CONTEXT for 4.1 (Q4.1.1-4.1.3): Monwabisi operates a trailer rental business. His rental costs for hiring a trailer are listed below: R1 000 refundable deposit per trailer if there is no damage to the trailer; R350 per day per small trailer; R500 per day per large trailer. TABLE 6 below shows the rental costs of trailers, including the deposit. [TABLE 6: RENTAL COSTS OF TRAILERS, WITH THE DEPOSIT INCLUDED. Number of days (n): 1, 3, 5, 7, 10, 15. Cost for small trailer: R1 350, R2 050, B, R3 450, R4 500, R6 250. Cost for large trailer: R1 500, R2 500, R3 500, R4 500, R6 000, R8 500.] [Adapted from www.getawaytrailers.co.za] Use TABLE 6 and the information above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION: Write down a formula to calculate the rental cost, including the deposit, of a large trailer in the form: Cost = ...
questions.memo_working: 1A deposit (R1 000); 1A variable cost (R500 x n). OR Cost = R1 000 + (R500 x number of days)

questions.text: [Context 4.1: trailer rental costs, TABLE 6 - see Q4.1.1] Calculate the missing value B.
questions.topic: Finance (tables of values from a cost model)
questions.memo_working: B = R1 000 + (R350 x 5) (1A, 1MA multiplying values) = R2 750 (1CA simplification). OR B = R2 050 + R350 + R350 (1A R2 050, 1MA adding values) = R2 750. AO

questions.text: [Context 4.1: trailer rental costs - see Q4.1.1] On 12 December 2024, Monwabisi rented out TWO small trailers and SIX large trailers to different customers for a day. One of the trailers was returned with a damaged rear light. (a) Monwabisi stated that his total income, after refunding the deposits, amounted to R4 550. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether his statement is VALID.
questions.memo_answer: Income for both trailer types = (R1 350 x 2) + (R1 500 x 6) = R11 700; total income after refunding 7 deposits = R11 700 - R7 000 = R4 700. Statement NOT VALID.
questions.memo_working: Income = (R1 350 x 2) + (R1 500 x 6) (1MA multiplying values) = R2 700 + R9 000 (1A) = R11 700 (1CA). Total income after refund = R11 700 - R7 000 (1MCA subtracting R7 000) = R4 700 (1CA). Statement NOT VALID (1O conclusion). OR rental income only = (R350 x 2) + (R500 x 6) = R700 + R3 000; plus retained deposit R1 000 = R4 700; NOT VALID
questions.memo_note: Seven of the eight R1 000 deposits are refunded; the deposit of the damaged trailer is retained.

questions.text: [Context 4.1: trailer rental costs - see Q4.1.3a] (b) The following quotation for the repair and replacement of the rear light was received: New rear light R242; Labour at R480 per hour or part thereof; Time required to complete the repair and replacement is 1 hour 30 minutes. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether the deposit amount will be sufficient to cover the total cost of the entire repair and replacement.
questions.memo_answer: Labour cost = R480 x 2 = R960; total cost = R960 + R242 = R1 202. The deposit of R1 000 will not be sufficient.
questions.memo_working: Labour cost = R480 x 2 (1MA multiplying by 2) = R960 (1CA simplification). Total cost = R960 + R242 = R1 202 (1CA simplification). The deposit of R1 000 will not be sufficient (1O conclusion). OR R1 000 - R480 - R480 - R242 = -R202 (1A R480, 1MCA, 1CA); not sufficient (1O)
questions.memo_note: 1 hour 30 minutes is charged as 2 hours ('per hour or part thereof').

questions.text: [Context 4.2: TABLE 7 VAT payments by sector - see Q4.2.1] Calculate (in R million) the mean VAT payment amount per economic sector.
[Context 4.2: TABLE 7 VAT payments by sector - see Q4.2.1] (a) Arrange the number of vendors in ascending order.
questions.memo_working: 1RT all correct values; 1A ascending order

questions.text: [Context 4.2: TABLE 7 VAT payments by sector - see Q4.2.4a] (b) The value of quartile 3 (Q3) for the number of vendors is 86 610. Calculate the interquartile range (IQR) for the number of vendors. You may use the following formula: Interquartile range (IQR) = Q3 - Q1
questions.memo_working: Q1 = 15 258 (1A). IQR = 86 610 - 15 258 (1MCA subtracting values) = 71 352 (1CA simplification). CA from Question 4.2.4(a)

questions.text: CONTEXT for 5.1 (Q5.1.1-5.1.3): Candice started a small delivery business in London and planned to purchase an electric car for the business. TABLE 8 below shows information on TWO car purchase options, A and B, that she could choose from. [TABLE 8: INFORMATION ON THE CAR PURCHASE OPTIONS. Picture of a Dolphin hatchback car. Rows (DETAILS | OPTION A | OPTION B): Payment period 48 months | 48 months; Deposit and first-month instalment £1 173,66 | £1 640,61; Additional months' instalment £195,61 | £182,29; Compulsory monthly maintenance cover £25,36 | £24,00.] [Adapted from www.leasecar.uk/car-leasing/byd/dolphin-hatchback] NOTE: All amounts exclude 20% VAT. Use TABLE 8 and the information above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION: Calculate the total maintenance cover for the payment period for OPTION B.
questions.memo_working: Total maintenance cover for option B = £24 x 48 (1RT £24) = £1 152 (1CA simplification). AO

questions.text: [Context 5.1: TABLE 8 car purchase options - see Q5.1.1] Candice chooses OPTION A. (a) Give ONE possible reason why Candice chose OPTION A.
questions.memo_answer: The deposit and first-month instalment is much lower. OR Option A has a smaller deposit.
questions.memo_working: 2O reason

questions.text: [Context 5.1: TABLE 8 car purchase options - see Q5.1.1] (b) Calculate the total amount, including VAT, that she would have paid at the end of the payment period.
questions.memo_working: Total price excluding VAT = £1 173,66 (1RT) + (£195,61 x 47) (1A 47 instalments) + (£25,36 x 48) (1A 48 maintenance payments) = £1 173,66 + £9 193,67 + £1 217,28 (1MCA adding all values) = £11 584,61 excl VAT (1CA). Total including VAT = £11 584,61 x 120/100 or x 1,2 (1MCA calculating VAT) = £13 901,53 (1CA total including VAT). OR VAT amount = £11 584,61 x 20/100 = £2 316,92; total = £11 584,61 + £2 316,92 = £13 901,53. OR each component x 1,2 then added: £1 408,39 + £11 032,40 + £1 460,74 = £13 901,53
questions.memo_note: 47 additional instalments because the first month's instalment is included in the deposit amount; maintenance cover runs for all 48 months.

questions.text: [Context 5.1: TABLE 8 car purchase options - see Q5.1.1] Candice's aunt in Switzerland offers to pay the deposit and first-month instalment. TABLE 9 below shows the currency conversion factors. [TABLE 9: CURRENCY CONVERSION FACTORS. Columns: CURRENCY | ZAR PER UNIT | UNITS PER ZAR. Rows: Swiss franc (CHF) 20,48 | 0,049; Pound sterling (£) 23,20 | 0,043.] [Adapted from www.xe.com/currencyconverter] Calculate, in Swiss franc (CHF), the deposit and first-month instalment for OPTION A.
questions.topic: Finance (currency conversion via a third currency)
questions.memo_answer: CHF 1 332,74 (alternatives in memo: CHF 1 337,43; CHF 1 329,54; CHF 1 334,22)
questions.memo_working: Deposit and first-month instalment = £1 173,66 (1RT). Amount in rand = £1 173,66 / 0,043 (1MA exchange rate) = R27 294,42 (1CA). Amount in CHF = R27 294,42 / R20,48 (1MCA exchange rate) = CHF 1 332,74 (1CA) OR R27 294,42 x 0,049 = CHF 1 337,43. OR via £1 173,66 x R23,20 = R27 228,91; /20,48 = CHF 1 329,54 OR x 0,049 = CHF 1 334,22. OR conversion rate £1 = CHF 23,20/20,48 = 1,1328125 (1MA, 1CA); 1 173,66 x 1,1328125 = CHF 1 329,54
questions.memo_note: The memo accepts several answers depending on which of the rounded conversion factors are used (1 329,54 / 1 332,74 / 1 334,22 / 1 337,43).

questions.text: CONTEXT for 5.2 (Q5.2.1-5.2.4): Candice's husband has a car with a 40 litre petrol tank capacity. The price of petrol may change from month to month. ANNEXURE B in the ANSWER BOOK shows the graph of the average petrol price per month in pounds (£) for a four-month period during 2024. [ANNEXURE B in Special Answer Book - not in repo. From memo usage: a line/bar graph of average petrol price per month for Jul.-Oct. 2024; Jul. 2024 reads £1,45 and Aug. 2024 reads about £1,42 (memo accepts readings 1,41-1,43).] TABLE 10 below shows the monthly inflation percentages for a four-month period during 2024. [TABLE 10: MONTHLY INFLATION RATES FOR THE PERIOD JUL. 2024 TO OCT. 2024. Jul. 2024: 2,2; Aug. 2024: 2,2; Sep. 2024: C; Oct. 2024: 2,3.] Use ANNEXURE B and the information above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION: The average inflation rate over the four-month period during 2024 was 2,1%. Calculate the missing value C.
questions.memo_working: 2,1 = (2,2 + 2,2 + 2,3 + C)/4 (1MA concept of mean; 1MA adding all values); 2,1 x 4 = 6,7 + C; C = 8,4% - 6,7% = 1,7% (1CA simplification). OR sum = 2,1 x 4 = 8,4% (1MA); C = 8,4% - 6,7% (1MA) = 1,7% (1CA). AO

questions.text: [Context 5.2: petrol prices, ANNEXURE B graph and TABLE 10 - see Q5.2.1] Candice stated that the difference in the cost of a full tank of petrol from Jul. 2024 to Aug. 2024, was £1,5. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether her statement is VALID. [ANNEXURE B in Special Answer Book - not in repo]
questions.memo_answer: Difference = (£1,45 - £1,42) x 40 ℓ = £1,20. Her statement is NOT VALID.
questions.memo_working: Difference = (£1,45 (1A) - £1,42 (1RT, graph reading; accept 1,41-1,43)) x 40 ℓ (1MA multiply difference with capacity) = £1,20 (1CA simplification). NOT VALID (1O conclusion). OR (£1,45 x 40) - (£1,42 x 40) = £58 - £56,80 (1MA) = £1,20 (1CA); NOT VALID (1O)
questions.memo_note: One of the two monthly prices is read from the missing ANNEXURE B graph (memo accepts 1,41-1,43); the arithmetic itself is verified.

questions.text: [Context 5.2: petrol prices, ANNEXURE B graph and TABLE 10 - see Q5.2.1] Calculate, in £ per litre, the cost of petrol during Jun. 2024, if the petrol price from Jun. 2024 to Jul. 2024 changed in line with inflation. [ANNEXURE B in Special Answer Book - not in repo]
questions.memo_working: Petrol price for June = £1,45 (1RT) x 100/102,2 OR £1,45/1,022 (1MA percentage calculation) = £1,42 (1CA simplification). AO. CA from Question 5.2.2
questions.memo_note: £1,45 is the Jul. 2024 reading from the missing ANNEXURE B graph; the reverse-inflation arithmetic (1,45/1,022 = 1,42) is verified.

questions.text: [Context 5.2: petrol prices, TABLE 10 - see Q5.2.1] Describe the trend in the inflation rate for the period Jul. 2024 to Oct. 2024.
questions.memo_answer: It remains the same (constant) for July to August; it decreases from August to September; it increases from September to October.
questions.memo_working: 1A remains the same; 1A decreases; 1A increases. (CA from Question 5.2.1)
